App is ok, but I really would prefer full access to the wash/rinse cycles without having to use an app. Even after all my gripes, I would buy again. Sentence (English): This could be the best dishwasher ever, but we'll never purchase from Home Depot again.
Comments (English): [ Done with Home Depot ] || ---------------- || This could be the best dishwasher ever, but we'll never purchase from Home Depot again. If you're building a new construction home, I would think long and hard before purchasing appliances from Home Depot. We went into the store on December 30th because they were having a buy more, save more sale, which was going to save us around $800 on our appliances. We spoke to the sales lady and told her that we weren't sure when we would be able to take delivery. She told us that it wouldn't be an issue and if we saw that our appliances were going to be delivered earlier than we needed, then all we had to do was call the 800 number and postpone it for as long as we needed. Delivery was set for the end of January and then moved to the end of February when we realized that the interior was taking longer than originally anticipated. The delivery company starts calling at the beginning of February and starts screaming at us about how they'll only hold our appliances for 30 days and wanted to know “what we were going to do about it”. We explained that we weren't ready for the delivery and that the store had told us that we could postpone it as long as we needed. They didn't care and told us that we could put it in a garage out of the way. It's a 900 square foot tiny home. There is no garage and no place out of the way. After speaking to a supervisor, they agreed to the original delivery date at the end of February. Following this conversation, our contractor's mother unfortunately passed away. While he was dealing with that, the wrong flooring was unintentionally ordered and installed. New flooring was going to take two weeks to arrive, which was after the appliances were set to be delivered. We went into Home Depot and talked to the customer service desk. They looked at the order and told us that there shouldn't be any reason why we couldn't move it back if we weren't ready, so we moved it back to March 7th. The delivery company called a few days later telling us that they weren't going to hold it and they didn't care what kind of delays we had because they weren't holding the appliances any longer. They were beyond rude. After speaking to a supervisor again and explaining that we had weeks of delays that were not our fault, he still wouldn't agree to wait for the delivery until he spoke with his supervisors. We then called the Home Depot customer service number and explained the situation. The rep seemed sympathetic and told me that she was going to call the delivery company and see why the couldn't hold them. She gets back on the line and completely changed her tone. She told us that it was the delivery company's policy to only hold our appliances 30 days and there was nothing she could do. She said that they were going to try to get us an exception, but she couldn't guarantee anything. We told her that we didn't purchase the appliances from the delivery company. We purchased them from Home Depot and we were told that we had as much time as we needed for the delivery. She didn't care and refused to help us out any further. The delivery company finally agreed to move the delivery to March 7th, but told us that they wouldn't move it out a day further. Not only did our flooring get delayed another week, but it came in with half the boxes crushed, further delaying our build. We didn't even call to have the appliances moved again, because we were tired of fighting with the delivery company and being threatened with canceling our order. Our appliances were delivered on March 7th. The guys who made the delivery did fine, but it's likely that our appliances will get damaged while flooring is still being installed, the interior painted, and the cabinets installed. Another big box home improvement store held my brother's appliances for 6 months while his home was being built, so I know it is done all the time. We will be using that store in the future. After spending $25,000 plus with Home Depot in the last two years, between our office remodel and this new construction, you would think that Home Depot might care a little more about maintaining good relationships with their customers, but it's obvious that they don't. We have since purchased the rest of our items from other stores who appreciate our business and will not be spending another dime with Home Depot in the future.

Comments (English): [ Software update required ] || ---------------- || I had the following experience with this product: the efficient dry function, which has 3 options (inactive, active for all programs or active only for the eco program), sometimes worked, sometimes not. I had preset a washing program in which the speed perfect function was also active, I also selected the efficient dry option active for all programs, the first efficient dry wash cycle worked, the next one it did not work anymore. The support people told me that efficient dry does not work together with speed perfect. Although the support people say that these 2 functions do not work together, they can still work together one time. It seems that there is a software limitation missing, I would say that if you activate one of the 2 functions, the other one automatically becomes inactive. From my point of view, a software update is necessary for this aspect. It took me 1 week of tests to figure out why it works once and then doesn't work again. Overall I am happy with the product, leaving aside the software limitation which could be improved with an update. It deserves 5 stars!

For those accustomed to using the upper rack for plastics and glassware - the utility of the space is better, but not much better than other units. Although expensive, this equipment provides good value; would happily purchase it again.

Sentence (English): Sixteen years ago, we bought a black Bosch dishwasher, and it recently broke down, likely due to a problem with the pump.
Comments (English): [ An exceptional dishwasher ] || ---------------- || Sixteen years ago, we bought a black Bosch dishwasher, and it recently broke down, likely due to a problem with the pump. We asked Bosch, and they offered to repair it with an authorized technician visiting for a very reasonable price. But after doing the math, we decided that maybe 16 years is too long, and it's better to replace the appliance with a new one, more energy-efficient, with an upper cutlery tray now that the family has grown, and with an automatic door opening. We looked at many, MANY models and brands, and in the end, we were torn between another black brand, a very expensive, high-end model, and this white Bosch, which clashes with the aesthetics of our kitchen, but with a much more reasonable price (almost half) and better features than the other option! The reliability of Bosch made us decide, and when we received it, we were still unsure if we had done the right thing, but after using it twice... and now we're sure it was the right choice! It's a dishwasher with Home Connect, which allows you to turn it on remotely (not something we're going to do) and view electricity and water consumption (it works great for us) and download or configure new programs. The wash cycle can be scheduled by hour, so you can run it at night when electricity is cheaper. Even in ECO mode, which isn't SILENCE mode, you can barely hear anything in the stillness of the early morning. Just a slight hum that can't be heard with the kitchen door closed. It's perfect for using during low-energy periods. The quick wash cycle lasts an hour and leaves dishes, pots, glasses, and cutlery clean and shiny. The drying process is simply impressive: if you set the automatic door opening, it consumes less energy and takes longer to dry, but the results are very, very good. However, with the dishwasher drying with the door closed, the results are EXCELLENT: the heat emanating when you open it is incomparable to my old model, and the glassware comes out dry, spotless, and sparkling clean. The cutlery tray is rigid and sturdy, like the other two; it's also removable in case you want to put something tall on the second one, which was a concern we had. The second tray has three heights, and it stays firm on all of them. It fits more plates and glasses than our old Bosch. For now, we're very, very happy. We just hope it lasts as long as our old one did, and that it doesn't give us the same problems—that is, none at all. As I said, the only downside is the color, but it was still a very good purchase, and we're more than satisfied. I hope we have Bosch for many, many years.
Comments (Original): [ Un lavavajillas excepcional ] || ---------------- || Hace 16 años compramos un lavavajillas Bosch de color negro, y recientemente nos falló, seguramente por un problema con la bomba. Preguntamos a Bosch y se ofrecieron a repararlo haciendo la visita el técnico oficial por un precio muy razonable, pero tras echar números pensamos que quizás 16 años ya son muchos, y mejor cambiar de aparato por uno nuevo, con mayor eficiencia energética, con bandeja superior para cubiertos ahora que la familia ha crecido, y con apertura automática de puerta.Miramos muchos, MUCHOS modelos y marcas, y al final dudábamos entre otra marca de color negro, modelo carísimo de gama altísima, y este Bosch, de color blanco que nos rompe con la estética de la cocina, pero con un precio mucho más ajustado (casi la mitad) y ¡mejores funciones que la otra opción!.Nos hizo decantarnos la fiabilidad que nos ha dado Bosch, y al recibirlo estábamos aún dubitativos de si habíamos hecho bien, pero ha sido usarlo dos veces… ¡y ya estamos seguros de que ha sido la opción correcta!.Es un lavavajillas con Home Connect, lo que permite desde encenderlo a distancia (no es algo que vayamos a hacer) hasta ver los consumo de energía eléctrica y agua (nos va genial) y descargar o configurar nuevos programas.El lavado se puede programar por horas, para dejarlo puesto de noche, cuando la luz es más barata, y aún en el modo ECO, que no es el modo SILENCE, no se escucha casi nada en la quietud de la madrugada. Sólo un ligero runrún que con la puerta de la cocina cerrada no se oye. Es perfecto para ponerlo en las franjas económicas de la luz.El ciclo de lavado rápido dura una hora y deja los platos, las ollas, los vasos y los cubiertos limpios y relucientes. El secado es simplemente impresionante: si pones apertura automática de puerta consume menos y tarda más en secar, pero los resultados son muy, muy buenos, pero es que con el secado del lavavajillas a puerta cerrada los resultados son EXCELENTES: el calor que emana al abrir no tiene punto de comparación con mi modelo antiguo, y la cristalería sale seca, sin mancha alguna y brillante.La bandeja de cubiertos es rígida y robusta, como las otras dos; además es extraíble por si quieres poner algo alto en la segunda, que es una duda que teníamos. La segunda bandeja tiene tres alturas, y en todas ellas se mantienen firmes.Caben más platos y vasos que en nuestro antiguo Bosch.De momento estamos muy, pero que muy contentos. Sólo esperamos que nos dure tanto como nos ha durado el antiguo, y que nos de los mismos problemas, es decir, ninguno. Como digo, la pena es el color, pero aún así ha sido una muy buena compra, y estamos más que satisfechos. Espero que tengamos Bosch para muchos, muchos años.

Sentence (English): This is a very efficient dishwasher which easily cleans and dries a full load on the economical 1 hour cycle.
Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher with lots of useful features - most importantly it cleans well ] || ---------------- || This is a very efficient dishwasher which easily cleans and dries a full load on the economical 1 hour cycle. The digital LED readout on the top of the door is a little hard to read however.We've been using the dishwasher for about a month now and it has performed well (but not flawlessly). We a household of two people, we fill it up and run it every 2-3 days and it handles all the glassware, plates, bowls and cutlery that we use in that time. We normally run it at night on the 1 hour cycle and everything is try and ready to unload on the following morning. We did have one disappointing experience with a bowl that had Bolognese sauce which we didn't rinse and it came out dirty following the longer Normal cycle. The manufacturer recommends rinsing any heavy residual from the dishware.Since the very top shelf is a cutlery rack, we removed the cutlery basket and use the extra space on the lower rack to accommodate more bowls and plates. The upper cutlery rack is very handy as you can keep the cutlery grouped as you load it which makes emptying the rack and refilling the cutlery drawer so much easier.There are some features that we really appreciate which drew us to this model, particularly the cycle which allows you to use citric acid to clean off lime scale build up from the interior every month or so. We have a well and the local water is hard which normally means the interior of our dishwasher is quite grubby after several months. There is a built-in Machine Clean reminder which illuminates on the control panel every 30 wash cycles to remind you to clean the tub and make sure the removable food particle filter is empty.Our kitchen and living area is open and we can run the dishwasher without too much noise interference. Our previous washer was a little quieter and the main difference with this one and our old one appears to be the thickness of the sound deadening pad which wraps around the outside of the tub. The main noise you hear is the occasional sound of water splashing around inside when the wash cycle begins. You can easily hold a conversation in the kitchen when it is running.Another feature I like is that you can adjust the amount of rinse aid that is used in a wash cycle. This is also helpful as we can increase the amount of rinse aid to compensate for the hardness in our well water.The dishwasher has the wash cycle options you would expect – 1 hour, normal, heavy soil, delicate and auto. It also has the option to boost the drying cycle and also accommodates a Night Dry option which will occasionally run the internal fan to minimize condensation when the dishes are washed overnight and not emptied until the following morning. If you want the dishwasher to start after you have gone out to work or gone to bed for the night, there is a delay start feature which allows the washing cycle to begin anywhere between 1 to 12 hours later.Another cool feature is the Flexible washing Zones which allows you to load the lower rack or the upper rack (or both) to save electric/water or deal with heavily soiled crockery and pans in the lower rack. The Flexible Zone directs more/less water to the racks for efficiency.The stainless steel finish is smudge resistant however if you spill cooking oil on it, the manufacturer recommends wiping those spills off immediately. The exterior finish can be cleaned with a soft, damp cloth or stainless steel cleaner. The interior can be cleaned with citric acid every 30 cycles and also with a cup of white vinegar left in a bowl in the upper rack.The dishwasher is also compatible with LG's free Thin-Q app which allows you to link the dishwasher to your home internet gateway and control some of the features (like turning it on and selecting the cycle options) from your smart phone. You can also download and control the half dozen or so custom cleaning cycles that are only accessible via the Thin-Q app. There is a QR code on a decal inside the door which makes pairing the Thin-Q app with the dishwasher more straightforward. While I understand that there are some occasional benefits to wifi/NFC connectivity (like realizing you forgot to switch the dishwasher on while you are out and about), this wasn't a major selling point for us. It will probably come in handy if we need to do any trouble shooting diagnosis as it also provides access to the maintenance features.Installation was pretty straightforward however I struggled to get the dishwasher level from front to back, even with the adjuster feet at their fullest extent. There was also a gap around the sides of the dishwasher where the black rubber gasket seal didn't quite reach the sides of the 24 ¼” opening in our kitchen cabinet (the dishwasher we removed filled this properly).The dishwasher is made in Korea and come with a 1 year parts/labor warranty (which includes on site service to replace any parts), a 2 year warranty for the main control board, racks, stainless steel door liner and tub (the customer pays for in-home service or labor to replace these parts) and a ten year warranty on the direct drive motor.

The digital LED readout on the top of the door is a little hard to read however.We've been using the dishwasher for about a month now and it has performed well (but not flawlessly). We a household of two people, we fill it up and run it every 2-3 days and it handles all the glassware, plates, bowls and cutlery that we use in that time. We normally run it at night on the 1 hour cycle and everything is try and ready to unload on the following morning. We did have one disappointing experience with a bowl that had Bolognese sauce which we didn't rinse and it came out dirty following the longer Normal cycle. The manufacturer recommends rinsing any heavy residual from the dishware.Since the very top shelf is a cutlery rack, we removed the cutlery basket and use the extra space on the lower rack to accommodate more bowls and plates. The upper cutlery rack is very handy as you can keep the cutlery grouped as you load it which makes emptying the rack and refilling the cutlery drawer so much easier.There are some features that we really appreciate which drew us to this model, particularly the cycle which allows you to use citric acid to clean off lime scale build up from the interior every month or so. We have a well and the local water is hard which normally means the interior of our dishwasher is quite grubby after several months. There is a built-in Machine Clean reminder which illuminates on the control panel every 30 wash cycles to remind you to clean the tub and make sure the removable food particle filter is empty.Our kitchen and living area is open and we can run the dishwasher without too much noise interference. Our previous washer was a little quieter and the main difference with this one and our old one appears to be the thickness of the sound deadening pad which wraps around the outside of the tub. The main noise you hear is the occasional sound of water splashing around inside when the wash cycle begins. You can easily hold a conversation in the kitchen when it is running.Another feature I like is that you can adjust the amount of rinse aid that is used in a wash cycle. This is also helpful as we can increase the amount of rinse aid to compensate for the hardness in our well water.The dishwasher has the wash cycle options you would expect – 1 hour, normal, heavy soil, delicate and auto. It also has the option to boost the drying cycle and also accommodates a Night Dry option which will occasionally run the internal fan to minimize condensation when the dishes are washed overnight and not emptied until the following morning. If you want the dishwasher to start after you have gone out to work or gone to bed for the night, there is a delay start feature which allows the washing cycle to begin anywhere between 1 to 12 hours later.Another cool feature is the Flexible washing Zones which allows you to load the lower rack or the upper rack (or both) to save electric/water or deal with heavily soiled crockery and pans in the lower rack. The Flexible Zone directs more/less water to the racks for efficiency.The stainless steel finish is smudge resistant however if you spill cooking oil on it, the manufacturer recommends wiping those spills off immediately. The exterior finish can be cleaned with a soft, damp cloth or stainless steel cleaner. The interior can be cleaned with citric acid every 30 cycles and also with a cup of white vinegar left in a bowl in the upper rack.The dishwasher is also compatible with LG's free Thin-Q app which allows you to link the dishwasher to your home internet gateway and control some of the features (like turning it on and selecting the cycle options) from your smart phone. You can also download and control the half dozen or so custom cleaning cycles that are only accessible via the Thin-Q app. There is a QR code on a decal inside the door which makes pairing the Thin-Q app with the dishwasher more straightforward. While I understand that there are some occasional benefits to wifi/NFC connectivity (like realizing you forgot to switch the dishwasher on while you are out and about), this wasn't a major selling point for us. It will probably come in handy if we need to do any trouble shooting diagnosis as it also provides access to the maintenance features.Installation was pretty straightforward however I struggled to get the dishwasher level from front to back, even with the adjuster feet at their fullest extent. There was also a gap around the sides of the dishwasher where the black rubber gasket seal didn't quite reach the sides of the 24 ¼” opening in our kitchen cabinet (the dishwasher we removed filled this properly).The dishwasher is made in Korea and come with a 1 year parts/labor warranty (which includes on site service to replace any parts), a 2 year warranty for the main control board, racks, stainless steel door liner and tub (the customer pays for in-home service or labor to replace these parts) and a ten year warranty on the direct drive motor.

We a household of two people, we fill it up and run it every 2-3 days and it handles all the glassware, plates, bowls and cutlery that we use in that time. We normally run it at night on the 1 hour cycle and everything is try and ready to unload on the following morning. We did have one disappointing experience with a bowl that had Bolognese sauce which we didn't rinse and it came out dirty following the longer Normal cycle. The manufacturer recommends rinsing any heavy residual from the dishware.Since the very top shelf is a cutlery rack, we removed the cutlery basket and use the extra space on the lower rack to accommodate more bowls and plates. The upper cutlery rack is very handy as you can keep the cutlery grouped as you load it which makes emptying the rack and refilling the cutlery drawer so much easier.There are some features that we really appreciate which drew us to this model, particularly the cycle which allows you to use citric acid to clean off lime scale build up from the interior every month or so. We have a well and the local water is hard which normally means the interior of our dishwasher is quite grubby after several months. There is a built-in Machine Clean reminder which illuminates on the control panel every 30 wash cycles to remind you to clean the tub and make sure the removable food particle filter is empty.Our kitchen and living area is open and we can run the dishwasher without too much noise interference. Our previous washer was a little quieter and the main difference with this one and our old one appears to be the thickness of the sound deadening pad which wraps around the outside of the tub. The main noise you hear is the occasional sound of water splashing around inside when the wash cycle begins. You can easily hold a conversation in the kitchen when it is running.Another feature I like is that you can adjust the amount of rinse aid that is used in a wash cycle. This is also helpful as we can increase the amount of rinse aid to compensate for the hardness in our well water.The dishwasher has the wash cycle options you would expect – 1 hour, normal, heavy soil, delicate and auto. It also has the option to boost the drying cycle and also accommodates a Night Dry option which will occasionally run the internal fan to minimize condensation when the dishes are washed overnight and not emptied until the following morning. If you want the dishwasher to start after you have gone out to work or gone to bed for the night, there is a delay start feature which allows the washing cycle to begin anywhere between 1 to 12 hours later.Another cool feature is the Flexible washing Zones which allows you to load the lower rack or the upper rack (or both) to save electric/water or deal with heavily soiled crockery and pans in the lower rack. The Flexible Zone directs more/less water to the racks for efficiency.The stainless steel finish is smudge resistant however if you spill cooking oil on it, the manufacturer recommends wiping those spills off immediately. The exterior finish can be cleaned with a soft, damp cloth or stainless steel cleaner. The interior can be cleaned with citric acid every 30 cycles and also with a cup of white vinegar left in a bowl in the upper rack.The dishwasher is also compatible with LG's free Thin-Q app which allows you to link the dishwasher to your home internet gateway and control some of the features (like turning it on and selecting the cycle options) from your smart phone. You can also download and control the half dozen or so custom cleaning cycles that are only accessible via the Thin-Q app. There is a QR code on a decal inside the door which makes pairing the Thin-Q app with the dishwasher more straightforward. While I understand that there are some occasional benefits to wifi/NFC connectivity (like realizing you forgot to switch the dishwasher on while you are out and about), this wasn't a major selling point for us. It will probably come in handy if we need to do any trouble shooting diagnosis as it also provides access to the maintenance features.Installation was pretty straightforward however I struggled to get the dishwasher level from front to back, even with the adjuster feet at their fullest extent. There was also a gap around the sides of the dishwasher where the black rubber gasket seal didn't quite reach the sides of the 24 ¼” opening in our kitchen cabinet (the dishwasher we removed filled this properly).The dishwasher is made in Korea and come with a 1 year parts/labor warranty (which includes on site service to replace any parts), a 2 year warranty for the main control board, racks, stainless steel door liner and tub (the customer pays for in-home service or labor to replace these parts) and a ten year warranty on the direct drive motor.

Sentence (English): The tines inside the lower shelf are to close together.
Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher for the most part. ] || ---------------- || The tines inside the lower shelf are to close together. Does not allow large bowls/pans. The one I had before had two row of tines that could turned down to all for large items. They could also be adjusted to slant several ways. This one has tines that are slanted but not adjustable. The second tier does go up and down easily. The second rack does raise and lower easily allowing for larger bottles/jars to fit over the jets. I do wish there was a way to not use the top and lower jets to allow a choice of using the top without the bottom jets. The dishwasher I had before this was a much better design inside. This new one has a better 3rd rack. The older one had a 3rd rack that was designed to put each piece of flatware in an individual slot. I do not know of anyone who ever took the time to place each one by one. This one has a flat rack too put large spoons or small items instead of flying around the inside of dishwasher. Since my electric company had many problems it killed the dishwasher and large refrigerator, too. Electronics do not like dirty electricity. Of course they are not responsible!

Easy to load / unload and it holds a lot. Many great optional settings, but I HATE that it relies on the app for so much of them. I would NOT recommend buying this model. I wish I had bought a different model that had more functions accessable from the control panel instead of my smart device. Seems that after the mechanical design was done, someone from marketing tried to figure out what valuable, but not essential functions to hold back for a subscription service. Why else would you omit button access to "delay start", " rinse only", etc ? One (and only one) cycle can be programmed into " favorite" button, but that only works with all selected options if triggered from within the app, not the button on the machine. This could probably all be fixed with a firmware update, but I can't see enough people complaining for Bosch to make this effort on an appliance that has already been sold. It's only a dishwasher. You can use it for full wash functions and it performs very well at that. No more pre rinsing anything! If you use your phone or voice activated device to set the temp on your oven when you use it, you will probably love this model.

Sentence (English): While moving, I searched to install an induction stove and dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ While I was moving, I searched to install an induction stove and dishwasher. Since they were more expensive to buy separately, I bought them as a set for about 1.23 million won on a live broadcast. The installation was done at a similar time, so it took about 3 hours. ] || ---------------- || While moving, I searched to install an induction stove and dishwasher. It would be more expensive if I bought them separately, so I bought them as a set for 1.23 million won on a live broadcast. The installation was done at a similar time and was completed in about 3 hours. The technicians who took care of the remodeling and installation were really kind and I asked them a lot of questions, and they explained everything in detail, which was nice. It was my first time using an induction stove and dishwasher, and it was a whole new world. First of all, the induction stove has a 3-burner glam gray color, so the design is luxurious and pretty. Also, the water boils quickly and the handle is not hot, so it is convenient. However, since I have only used gas stoves, I am still unfamiliar with the intensity control. I think I will get used to this part as I cook. The dishwasher is for 14 people, so it can hold plenty of dishes and pots, and it is not very noisy. However, I can definitely see why people prefer the hot air drying function. There is an automatic door opening function, but the water does not dry well. I was disappointed because there was still moisture even when I checked it at lunch the next day. But I think the results may vary depending on the detergent (rinse X or all-in-one product). Still, I think it was a really good purchase to be able to buy an induction and dishwasher together at this price :)
Comments (Original): [ 이사하는 김에 인덕션과 식기세척기를 설치하려고 검색했어요. 따로 구매하면 더 비싸서 라이브 방송에서 세트로 123만 원대에 구매했어요.설치는 비슷한 시간대에 진행해서 약 3시간 만 ] || ---------------- || 이사하는 김에 인덕션과 식기세척기를 설치하려고 검색했어요. 따로 구매하면 더 비싸서 라이브 방송에서 세트로 123만 원대에 구매했어요.설치는 비슷한 시간대에 진행해서 약 3시간 만에 끝났어요. 리폼과 설치를 맡아주신 기사님들은 정말 친절하셨고 궁금한 점을 많이 물어봤는데 하나하나 상세하게 설명해주셔서 좋았어요.저는 인덕션과 식기세척기를 처음 사용해봤는데, 완전 신세계더라고요.일단 인덕션은 3구짜리 글램 그레이 색상이라 디자인이 고급스럽고 예뻐요. 그리고 물이 빠르게 끓고 손잡이가 뜨겁지 않아서 편리해요. 다만, 저는 가스레인지만 사용해왔던 터라 세기 조절이 아직 낯설어요. 이 부분은 요리하면서 점점 익숙해질 것 같아요.식기세척기는 14인용이라 그릇과 냄비도 넉넉하게 들어가고 소음도 크지 않아요. 하지만 사람들이 왜 열풍건조 기능을 선호하는지 확실히 알겠더라고요. 자동문열림 기능이 있긴 한데 물이 잘 마르지 않아요. 다음 날 점심에 확인해도 물기가 남아 있어 아쉬웠어요. 근데 세척 세제(린스 X 또는 올인원 제품)에 따라 결과가 달라질 수도 있을 것 같다는 생각이 들어요.그래도 이 가격에 인덕션과 식기세척기를 함께 구매할 수 있었다니! 정말 잘 산 것 같아요:)

Overall, it can be a good choice if you want to maintain a clean kitchen while also having basic washing functions.

Comments (English): [ Keep your chopper bike—here's the chopper I like! ] || ---------------- || Bought the machine not on this platform but right from Maytag itself, but Best Buy probably has the most publicly visible site for me to review it on.Love this washer. Installed it myself and have had it in use for a couple of years now. So far it's proven very reliable. I find that it cleans by far the best of any of the several I've used. But still, per expert testing, some others clean a bit better. It's also very quiet in use. But still, per expert testing, some others are a bit quieter. But I love it just the same and chose it above all others I could find, because of its “food chopper,” a waste disposer built right in that is said to be the best on the market. So far as I can discern, many dishwashers have no such device, and no European one does, even Miele's high-end offerings.I always took the trouble to scrape and wipe down everything I put into my previous dishwashers, none of which was a Maytag. Yet, when I gave any of them a tedious thorough annual cleaning, I always found that each had a lot of debris clogging up its nether regions. Not so with this Maytag.With my previous washers, I'd take the time to tidy up the shootin' match. Once each year I'd pull out the filter, screen, spray arms, and associated parts, power-spray those parts all out thoroughly, scrub out the machine's interior, clear the guts out as far as I could reach my fingers in (right down to the drain-pump impeller), replace the removed parts, and then run the empty washer through a full cycle on the extra-hot setting with a container of special-purpose commercial cleanser. Quarterly, I'd empty it and run it through a full extra-hot cycle with an ounce of plain citric acid too. Between regular wash cycles, I'd rinse the contents all the time when it was partly filled to boot. No good neglecting it! But, even so, after another year had passed, each of my previous washers would once again be not just grimy, but cruddy. And, much more frequently than that, some of the holes in its spray arms would clog up and need clearing out. And, no matter how well maintained, no matter what detergent I used, my previous washers would at best do a good but not very good job of cleaning dishes in the bottom rack, and a so-so job in the top one.Even this machine I'll still run a package of dishwasher cleanser through annually, but I think I'm done with the dreary laborious hand-scrubs and sprayouts. I still scrape and wipe everything down before I put it in too, so as not to overwork the machinery, but it's nice to know it can probably handle any bits I happen to miss and will vigorously empty out the wash water instead of just slowly draining it. I treasure that vigor, and the food chopper as well, even though I've never owned a sink-drain-mounted waste disposer, for I have composted all my kitchen food waste for many years. I do occasionally find a scrap of food in this machine's “foreign object cup,” at the bottom close to the front and easily emptied.Some may prefer top-mounted controls over this machine's face-mounted ones, but I have no preference, and I like having a front-facing screen that tells me how long a time a cycle has yet to run. Some think this machine's full cycles take too long, but they don't trouble me at all; this machine does have a quick cycle, but the full-length cycles are pretty much all that I use at any time of day. Often the cycle finishes a little sooner than the countdown time first shown on the display.The Power Blast cycle is great for hard-to-clean items; in my experience, set-in strong tea stains and stainless-steel coffee stains are about the only things that may defeat it when I use a Finish Quantum pack in the dispenser, together with a little citric acid, and Cascade Complete powder in the pre-wash receptacle above it. (Other products may work just as well, but I happen to have a stock at home of the ones I mention. Detergents made today are at the cleaning disadvantage that they're prohibited from containing phosphates.) I do arrange everything I put in with some care—for the spray arms turn counterclockwise, as seen from above—and it all comes out quite clean despite that it's dry to start with, since I run the machine only once a week or so and never bother rinsing the contents between washes anymore.There are lots of settings besides, including optional drying with heat of long or short duration, which I very seldom use, and a menu of adjustable default settings. What's more, the machine's initial cost is modest and its ownership cost moderate. Really, the only feature found on other Maytag dishwashers that I wish this model had is a height adjustment for the upper rack. Some prefer a third rack, but I think that would be intrusive.My sole complaint probably applies to every dishwasher made today: Together with its stainless interior, I wish this machine's racks were made of stainless steel, not just coated, for I've found that the coating can crack off and allow the rack to rust, especially at the tines. But appliance-store sales staff assure me that nobody makes a dishwasher with stainless racks, and I suspect that the time it takes them to rust much is usually beyond any washer's expected service life. But I keep my dishwashing machines for many years.Bravo, Maytag, especially on your food chopper, and keep it up! Maytag's phone service these days does leave something to be desired. In my recent experience, a voice call with a general question may leave you trying to make your way through the phone tree to reach a live agent, calling repeatedly, and having long waits on hold, while a general email may be acknowledged but go unanswered.

Installed it myself and have had it in use for a couple of years now. So far it's proven very reliable. I find that it cleans by far the best of any of the several I've used. But still, per expert testing, some others clean a bit better. It's also very quiet in use. But still, per expert testing, some others are a bit quieter. But I love it just the same and chose it above all others I could find, because of its “food chopper,” a waste disposer built right in that is said to be the best on the market. So far as I can discern, many dishwashers have no such device, and no European one does, even Miele's high-end offerings.I always took the trouble to scrape and wipe down everything I put into my previous dishwashers, none of which was a Maytag. Yet, when I gave any of them a tedious thorough annual cleaning, I always found that each had a lot of debris clogging up its nether regions. Not so with this Maytag.With my previous washers, I'd take the time to tidy up the shootin' match. Once each year I'd pull out the filter, screen, spray arms, and associated parts, power-spray those parts all out thoroughly, scrub out the machine's interior, clear the guts out as far as I could reach my fingers in (right down to the drain-pump impeller), replace the removed parts, and then run the empty washer through a full cycle on the extra-hot setting with a container of special-purpose commercial cleanser. Quarterly, I'd empty it and run it through a full extra-hot cycle with an ounce of plain citric acid too. Between regular wash cycles, I'd rinse the contents all the time when it was partly filled to boot. No good neglecting it! But, even so, after another year had passed, each of my previous washers would once again be not just grimy, but cruddy. And, much more frequently than that, some of the holes in its spray arms would clog up and need clearing out. And, no matter how well maintained, no matter what detergent I used, my previous washers would at best do a good but not very good job of cleaning dishes in the bottom rack, and a so-so job in the top one.Even this machine I'll still run a package of dishwasher cleanser through annually, but I think I'm done with the dreary laborious hand-scrubs and sprayouts. I still scrape and wipe everything down before I put it in too, so as not to overwork the machinery, but it's nice to know it can probably handle any bits I happen to miss and will vigorously empty out the wash water instead of just slowly draining it. I treasure that vigor, and the food chopper as well, even though I've never owned a sink-drain-mounted waste disposer, for I have composted all my kitchen food waste for many years. I do occasionally find a scrap of food in this machine's “foreign object cup,” at the bottom close to the front and easily emptied.Some may prefer top-mounted controls over this machine's face-mounted ones, but I have no preference, and I like having a front-facing screen that tells me how long a time a cycle has yet to run. Some think this machine's full cycles take too long, but they don't trouble me at all; this machine does have a quick cycle, but the full-length cycles are pretty much all that I use at any time of day. Often the cycle finishes a little sooner than the countdown time first shown on the display.The Power Blast cycle is great for hard-to-clean items; in my experience, set-in strong tea stains and stainless-steel coffee stains are about the only things that may defeat it when I use a Finish Quantum pack in the dispenser, together with a little citric acid, and Cascade Complete powder in the pre-wash receptacle above it. (Other products may work just as well, but I happen to have a stock at home of the ones I mention. Detergents made today are at the cleaning disadvantage that they're prohibited from containing phosphates.) I do arrange everything I put in with some care—for the spray arms turn counterclockwise, as seen from above—and it all comes out quite clean despite that it's dry to start with, since I run the machine only once a week or so and never bother rinsing the contents between washes anymore.There are lots of settings besides, including optional drying with heat of long or short duration, which I very seldom use, and a menu of adjustable default settings. What's more, the machine's initial cost is modest and its ownership cost moderate. Really, the only feature found on other Maytag dishwashers that I wish this model had is a height adjustment for the upper rack. Some prefer a third rack, but I think that would be intrusive.My sole complaint probably applies to every dishwasher made today: Together with its stainless interior, I wish this machine's racks were made of stainless steel, not just coated, for I've found that the coating can crack off and allow the rack to rust, especially at the tines. But appliance-store sales staff assure me that nobody makes a dishwasher with stainless racks, and I suspect that the time it takes them to rust much is usually beyond any washer's expected service life. But I keep my dishwashing machines for many years.Bravo, Maytag, especially on your food chopper, and keep it up! Maytag's phone service these days does leave something to be desired. In my recent experience, a voice call with a general question may leave you trying to make your way through the phone tree to reach a live agent, calling repeatedly, and having long waits on hold, while a general email may be acknowledged but go unanswered.

The installer, the repair technician, and Coupang Media are all putting it off. No one is taking responsibility, and time is just passing. (It's a strong smell that makes you think it's carcinogenic.) The repair technician visited, but he inspected it several times. Before the technician arrived, there was a burning smell in Samsung and LG dishwasher cases. (Search "dishwasher burning smell" on Naver for examples.) However, they said the smell would get worse if they replaced it and it wouldn't help. I've used both Samsung and LG dishwashers. Ultimately, they're just like cars, with random shipping. This case clearly appears to be a product defect, and I believe an exchange or refund is necessary. I'll ask Coupang and the media. Regardless of whether it's a cost-effective, inexpensive product or an expensive one, I believe it's important to address any defects in products sold, rather than ignore them. I hope other consumers will carefully consider their purchases to avoid repeating the same burnt smell. If an exchange or refund isn't possible, I will report this to the Consumer Complaint Center and the media.

Comments (English): [ The worst dishwasher that doesn't dry at all ] || ---------------- || I don't usually write reviews, but I am writing this in the hopes that no one else becomes a victim like me. Even when I press the "Add Powerful Dry" button, nothing works at all. When I used products from other brands before, everything was fluffy and dry the moment the door opened (this is my third dishwasher, and even though the brands were weaker than this one, I was very satisfied with the dishwashers themselves). With this one, everything—whether it's ceramic dishes or anything else—dries completely, as if a bucket of water had just been poured over them. I've tried running small loads and adding extra drying settings, but nothing works. When I contacted them to complain, they said that Samsung products are designed to dry using hot water, so I have to air dry them. Then they should have stated that drying doesn't work. Sentence (English): This is a very efficient dishwasher which easily cleans and dries a full load on the economical 1 hour cycle.
Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher with lots of useful features - most importantly it cleans well ] || ---------------- || This is a very efficient dishwasher which easily cleans and dries a full load on the economical 1 hour cycle. The digital LED readout on the top of the door is a little hard to read however. We've been using the dishwasher for about a month now and it has performed well (but not flawlessly). We a household of two people, we fill it up and run it every 2-3 days and it handles all the glassware, plates, bowls and cutlery that we use in that time. We normally run it at night on the 1 hour cycle and everything is try and ready to unload on the following morning. We did have one disappointing experience with a bowl that had Bolognese sauce which we didn't rinse and it came out dirty following the longer Normal cycle. The manufacturer recommends rinsing any heavy residual from the dishware. Since the very top shelf is a cutlery rack, we removed the cutlery basket and use the extra space on the lower rack to accommodate more bowls and plates. The upper cutlery rack is very handy as you can keep the cutlery grouped as you load it which makes emptying the rack and refilling the cutlery drawer so much easier. There are some features that we really appreciate which drew us to this model, particularly the cycle which allows you to use citric acid to clean off lime scale build up from the interior every month or so. We have a well and the local water is hard which normally means the interior of our dishwasher is quite grubby after several months. There is a built-in Machine Clean reminder which illuminates on the control panel every 30 wash cycles to remind you to clean the tub and make sure the removable food particle filter is empty. Our kitchen and living area is open and we can run the dishwasher without too much noise interference. Our previous washer was a little quieter and the main difference with this one and our old one appears to be the thickness of the sound deadening pad which wraps around the outside of the tub. The main noise you hear is the occasional sound of water splashing around inside when the wash cycle begins. You can easily hold a conversation in the kitchen when it is running. Another feature I like is that you can adjust the amount of rinse aid that is used in a wash cycle. This is also helpful as we can increase the amount of rinse aid to compensate for the hardness in our well water. The dishwasher has the wash cycle options you would expect – 1 hour, normal, heavy soil, delicate and auto. It also has the option to boost the drying cycle and also accommodates a Night Dry option which will occasionally run the internal fan to minimize condensation when the dishes are washed overnight and not emptied until the following morning. If you want the dishwasher to start after you have gone out to work or gone to bed for the night, there is a delay start feature which allows the washing cycle to begin anywhere between 1 to 12 hours later. Another cool feature is the Flexible washing Zones which allows you to load the lower rack or the upper rack (or both) to save electric/water or deal with heavily soiled crockery and pans in the lower rack. The Flexible Zone directs more/less water to the racks for efficiency. The stainless steel finish is smudge resistant however if you spill cooking oil on it, the manufacturer recommends wiping those spills off immediately. The exterior finish can be cleaned with a soft, damp cloth or stainless steel cleaner. The interior can be cleaned with citric acid every 30 cycles and also with a cup of white vinegar left in a bowl in the upper rack. The dishwasher is also compatible with LG's free Thin-Q app which allows you to link the dishwasher to your home internet gateway and control some of the features (like turning it on and selecting the cycle options) from your smart phone. You can also download and control the half dozen or so custom cleaning cycles that are only accessible via the Thin-Q app. There is a QR code on a decal inside the door which makes pairing the Thin-Q app with the dishwasher more straightforward. While I understand that there are some occasional benefits to wifi/NFC connectivity (like realizing you forgot to switch the dishwasher on while you are out and about), this wasn't a major selling point for us. It will probably come in handy if we need to do any trouble shooting diagnosis as it also provides access to the maintenance features. Installation was pretty straightforward however I struggled to get the dishwasher level from front to back, even with the adjuster feet at their fullest extent. There was also a gap around the sides of the dishwasher where the black rubber gasket seal didn't quite reach the sides of the 24 ¼” opening in our kitchen cabinet (the dishwasher we removed filled this properly). The dishwasher is made in Korea and come with a 1 year parts/labor warranty (which includes on site service to replace any parts), a 2 year warranty for the main control board, racks, stainless steel door liner and tub (the customer pays for in-home service or labor to replace these parts) and a ten year warranty on the direct drive motor.

We normally run it at night on the 1 hour cycle and everything is try and ready to unload on the following morning. We did have one disappointing experience with a bowl that had Bolognese sauce which we didn’t rinse and it came out dirty following the longer Normal cycle. The digital LED readout on the top of the door is a little hard to read however. We've been using the dishwasher for about a month now and it has performed well (but not flawlessly). We a household of two people, we fill it up and run it every 2-3 days and it handles all the glassware, plates, bowls and cutlery that we use in that time. We normally run it at night on the 1 hour cycle and everything is try and ready to unload on the following morning. We did have one disappointing experience with a bowl that had Bolognese sauce which we didn't rinse and it came out dirty following the longer Normal cycle. The manufacturer recommends rinsing any heavy residual from the dishware. Since the very top shelf is a cutlery rack, we removed the cutlery basket and use the extra space on the lower rack to accommodate more bowls and plates. The upper cutlery rack is very handy as you can keep the cutlery grouped as you load it which makes emptying the rack and refilling the cutlery drawer so much easier. There are some features that we really appreciate which drew us to this model, particularly the cycle which allows you to use citric acid to clean off lime scale build up from the interior every month or so. We have a well and the local water is hard which normally means the interior of our dishwasher is quite grubby after several months. There is a built-in Machine Clean reminder which illuminates on the control panel every 30 wash cycles to remind you to clean the tub and make sure the removable food particle filter is empty. Our kitchen and living area is open and we can run the dishwasher without too much noise interference. Our previous washer was a little quieter and the main difference with this one and our old one appears to be the thickness of the sound deadening pad which wraps around the outside of the tub. The main noise you hear is the occasional sound of water splashing around inside when the wash cycle begins. You can easily hold a conversation in the kitchen when it is running. Another feature I like is that you can adjust the amount of rinse aid that is used in a wash cycle. This is also helpful as we can increase the amount of rinse aid to compensate for the hardness in our well water. The dishwasher has the wash cycle options you would expect – 1 hour, normal, heavy soil, delicate and auto. It also has the option to boost the drying cycle and also accommodates a Night Dry option which will occasionally run the internal fan to minimize condensation when the dishes are washed overnight and not emptied until the following morning. If you want the dishwasher to start after you have gone out to work or gone to bed for the night, there is a delay start feature which allows the washing cycle to begin anywhere between 1 to 12 hours later. Another cool feature is the Flexible washing Zones which allows you to load the lower rack or the upper rack (or both) to save electric/water or deal with heavily soiled crockery and pans in the lower rack. The Flexible Zone directs more/less water to the racks for efficiency. The stainless steel finish is smudge resistant however if you spill cooking oil on it, the manufacturer recommends wiping those spills off immediately. The exterior finish can be cleaned with a soft, damp cloth or stainless steel cleaner. The interior can be cleaned with citric acid every 30 cycles and also with a cup of white vinegar left in a bowl in the upper rack. The dishwasher is also compatible with LG's free Thin-Q app which allows you to link the dishwasher to your home internet gateway and control some of the features (like turning it on and selecting the cycle options) from your smart phone. You can also download and control the half dozen or so custom cleaning cycles that are only accessible via the Thin-Q app. There is a QR code on a decal inside the door which makes pairing the Thin-Q app with the dishwasher more straightforward. While I understand that there are some occasional benefits to wifi/NFC connectivity (like realizing you forgot to switch the dishwasher on while you are out and about), this wasn't a major selling point for us. It will probably come in handy if we need to do any trouble shooting diagnosis as it also provides access to the maintenance features. Installation was pretty straightforward however I struggled to get the dishwasher level from front to back, even with the adjuster feet at their fullest extent. There was also a gap around the sides of the dishwasher where the black rubber gasket seal didn't quite reach the sides of the 24 ¼” opening in our kitchen cabinet (the dishwasher we removed filled this properly). The dishwasher is made in Korea and come with a 1 year parts/labor warranty (which includes on site service to replace any parts), a 2 year warranty for the main control board, racks, stainless steel door liner and tub (the customer pays for in-home service or labor to replace these parts) and a ten year warranty on the direct drive motor.

Sentence (English): We bought the series 800 dishwasher as a replacement to an older Bosch model.
Comments (English): [ Bosch Dishwasher - Good and Bad ] || ---------------- || We bought the series 800 dishwasher as a replacement to an older Bosch model. The good: The dishwasher cleans very well and is super quiet. It is connected online so I get notifications when it is finished washing or needs Jet-Dry product or a deep clean run. The bad - the dishwasher feels flimsy when you open it to load. I thought several times I broke it when I grabbed it incorrectly to pull it open. The silverware basket (which we prefer) is super small compared to the previous models. There are some days where I have to run half the silverware in the next load which is disappointing. The dishwasher also does not auto-start if you have to open it mid cycle to put something in you forgot. You have to actually press a button or resume it in the app. Our older model auto-started so this is disappointing as well. Bosch spoiled us with features in a much older model then doubled the price and removed the great features it once had. We felt disappointed overall because of this with our choise and will certainly shop around next time we need a replacement.

Honestly, avoid the headache if you want clean dishes.

Comments (English): [ Bosch 800 Dishwasher after 1 month ] || ---------------- || 1 month into using my new Basch 800 dishwasher I'm glad I stuck with a Bosch. After setting everything up in the HomeConnect app, I realized I cannot use the control panel to delay start a load, it has to be done through the app. My second complaint is that while the light is on when the unit is running, there's no way to tell when a load is clean (finished running) or dirty without opening the door or looking at the app. Turning the light from white (running) to green (finished cleaning) would be beneficial. Otherwise, its a great upgrade.

Sentence (English): I did a great deal of research before purchasing my new dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ Cycle Time ] || ---------------- || I did a great deal of research before purchasing my new dishwasher. I have previously owned a KitchenAid and they continue to have a great reputation. I went to the store twice and opened and closed the door, pulled the racks out and even brought dishes to make sure they would fit as I wanted. What I didn't do was check to see how long the normal wash cycle would take. My previous dishwasher ran for a little over an hour. This one runs for 3 HOURS using normal wash and standard dry. I think that is ridiculous. And I won't use the express cycle because of the additional gallons of water it uses. I don't understand why it takes so long to run. I also don't like the fact that the silverware holder is on the right side which is the furthest away from me as I stand at the sink to load the dishwasher. I wish there was the flexibility to relocate it where it would best suit me but it is too wide to go anywhere else. The dishes are clean and dry but I don't like the length of the cycle and the extra expense in operating the machine.

Sentence (English): This dishwasher was purchased new and already came with manufacturer problems.
Comments (English): [ Cheap plastic parts ] || ---------------- || This dishwasher was purchased new and already came with manufacturer problems. There is a part at the bottom that diverts water to the spray arms that is faulty. It is made of cheap plastic and does not stay seated. So, after 3.5 hours of washing time, you still have dirty dishes. Everything has to be taken out of the dishwasher on the bottom, the UR PORT DIVERTER WITH DISC AND MAGNET KIT has to be reseated, then you may get another 2 washes, then have to repeat. There is no screw or bolt to hold latch into place, just a flimsy piece of plastic. This is not what you would expect out of a higher end appliance. Oh, you only get a 1 year warranty as well, so, once the plastic completely fails, tough luck! So, no, I do not recommend this dishwasher. Poorly made with a hefty price tag.

Comments (English): [ Best value for money, but the downsides are visible when compared to SK** ] || ---------------- || I'm "Review Kong," a company that writes only honest reviews. I've been using an SK** dishwasher. These days, electronic devices are supposed to last exactly five years, so after six years, it started malfunctioning, popping up an error code. The parts alone cost 160,000 won, and they wouldn't arrive until three weeks later. They said even after replacing the parts, there was no guarantee it wouldn't break again in a year or two, so I immediately looked into buying a dishwasher. I'd heard so many times that detergent and rinse were more important than the price of the dishwasher. When I first used an SK**, I bought a really good, expensive one, but I used random detergent, and the water stains stayed the same. I was incredibly disappointed with the dishwasher. Dishwasher = Good Detergent & Rinse I looked into Coupang for dishwashers because of their "rocket installation" and "free warranty." I also hoped they'd remove my broken dishwasher for free. I bought it the night before, and they installed it the next morning at 9:00. It was truly rocket installation. It's truly the best. After installing the 12-seater Media dishwasher, let me compare it to the SK**. First, the cleaning performance is similar. It washes well and removes grease well. The only downside is that the dish tray is noticeably cheap. It wobbles a lot, should I say? It feels incredibly light. When you slide it in and out, it feels heavier than the SK**. That's the difference. The old SK** had two rotating wash wings, one at the top and one at the bottom, while the Media dishwasher has them in the middle and bottom. The drying section is also a bit disappointing. The door opens automatically, but it doesn't open very far. Because of this, even after 12 hours, water builds up inside, and dishes don't dry completely. That's a real downside. However, at this price, I think it's a much better deal than having to worry about replacing parts and potentially breaking down. I highly recommend it to anyone buying a dishwasher for the first time. Just because it's expensive doesn't mean it's good! Dishwashers are always meant to be used with detergent.

Sentence (English): I used to use a 12-place setting LG dishwasher.
Comments (English): [ It is perfect for a family of three. ] || ---------------- || I used to use a 12-place setting LG dishwasher. However, as a family of three, there were many days when I ran it because the amount of dishes I collected all day was so small. Whenever we moved, restoring the base cabinets and reinstalling the dishwasher was a hassle and a hassle. Also, the parts removed from the base cabinets had to be stored to be restored when we moved out, but they were heavy and bulky, which was a burden. After using it for about five years, the compartments started breaking here and there, and it beeped frequently; it seemed like it was malfunctioning. So, during this move, I boldly threw it away and bought a 6-place setting model. My husband was worried that I might regret going from a 12-place setting to a 6-place one because it felt too small. But since I really pursue a minimalist lifestyle and like things simple, I figured if space is tight, I can just quickly wash a few dishes! So I went ahead and bought it. The most important feature for me was the automatic door opening function. Since the door needs to open automatically to allow the dishes to circulate and dry overnight, preventing bacterial growth, this was an essential feature. That is why I chose this product, and the technician installed it perfectly on the day of the move. I am currently getting used to how to Tetris the dishes by arranging them this way and that to get the fit right. Since washing cups by hand seems like the best way to save space, I plan to skip putting them in starting tomorrow. If guests come over and the amount of food increases, I can just run it twice anyway. I really love it. I hope my review was helpful.

Sentence (English): It came delivered packaged well and in good condition.
Comments (English): [ Good dishwasher but lacks in some functionality ] || ---------------- || It came delivered packaged well and in good condition. I got a good deal and was happy to have the stainless steel inside over the plastic. It functions as a dishwasher, and does better than my old one at getting the dishes clean. It is much more quiet than our old one, so that was nice because I wasn't necessarily expecting that. However, my two issues. One, the third rack on the very top limits the cups and bowls that can be placed in the top rack. So much so I took it out. It is just not practical. Secondly, our old dishwasher had a holder for silverware in the front of the bottom drawer, which made it easy to open the door, drop your silverware in, and close it. This new one has that on the side, so you have to open up the door and then pull out the bottom rack. The slots are also a bit smaller than I think they should be, and some of the handles on our larger silverware do not fit. This is a bummer. Because of these issues, I want to rate this three stars, but I give a star back because it is more quiet than I was expecting when running a cycle. It does seem built well to boot and without the top rack, fits our dishes nicely. All in all, I'm happy with the price we paid and what we got.

Sentence (English): On February 17, I purchased three large household appliances— a washing machine, a dryer, and a dishwasher— from bestbuy.
Comments (English): [ After Sales Nightmare ] || ---------------- || On February 17, I purchased three large household appliances— a washing machine, a dryer, and a dishwasher— from Best Buy. To ensure everything would be perfect, I also bought an extended warranty. Since I'm capable of handling it myself, I declined the installation service because, unfortunately, I'm not satisfied with the workmanship of most installation services.The first shock came the day after my purchase when I received a text message asking me to reschedule the service appointment initially set for March 11. The earliest available date was April 2— 44 days after my purchase! The second shock was realizing that the appliances didn't come with the necessary installation parts. I made this purchase through Best Buy's live web chat with a sales representative, opting only to exclude the installation labor. It never crossed my mind that these machines would arrive without such essential components. These weren't accessories but necessary parts for operation! The sales representative never warned me that I would need to purchase them separately. Moreover, the order confirmation screenshot sent by the representative clearly stated, “This item has services and parts included! ”The third shock happened on the scheduled service day. While randomly checking my Best Buy account, I noticed an open slot for March 14. I immediately rescheduled my appointment, and the service team confirmed via text message that they would arrive at 10 AM. I adjusted my schedule accordingly. However, Best Buy's partner, Lone Star Overnight (LSO), kept pushing back the service time— first to 11 AM, then 12 PM, and finally 1 PM. I couldn't wait at home any longer, so I had to leave, leaving my two daughters— one older and one younger— at home. The service team finally arrived at 1:26 PM, which I later confirmed through my security cameras.The fourth shock was the rudeness and carelessness of the service team. Even though my daughters asked the technician to wear shoe covers inside the house, he repeatedly stepped outside wearing them and then walked back in, which I could see from the cameras, along with the annoyed expression on his face. I also noticed that the appliances were delivered without packaging! (Could they have been display models and open box? ) Since I saw this on the cameras, I asked my daughters to closely monitor the technician and check for any visible damage. When I got home, my daughters told me that the technician struggled to move all three appliances by himself and that one machine scraped against the wall during transportation. However, since he didn't take our questions seriously, they hesitated to object and say, “We don't want this in this condition! ” Instead, they simply took a picture of the damage.The fifth shock came from the response of Best Buy's customer service representatives when I shared this terrible experience via text, phone calls, and web chat. • I was told, “We're handling it immediately, you'll be called today.” Yet, when Best Buy never called, these conversations continued with different representatives for three days, repeating the same sentences over and over. • Even after I sent a photo of the damaged machine still on the moving cart, one representative had the audacity to say, “How do we know you didn't do this? ” • I was told, “You need to bring the machine to us; we can't pick it up. Once you bring it in, you can receive a replacement.” • Despite the order stating, “This item has services and parts included” I was told, “Sorry, you have to purchase them” when I asked about the washer's hot and cold water inlet hoses and the dryer's power cord. For an additional cost that was only about 1% of the total purchase price, these sales representatives showed no effort or initiative to resolve a disappointed customer's frustration.In short, since we expected our new machines to arrive, we got rid of our old ones. Since that day, we haven't been able to do laundry at home.We are still waiting for our new machine.If I experienced all of this just during the initial purchase, I don't even want to imagine what I might go through during the five-year warranty period.It was a terrible experience. I think my next purchase won't be from Best Buy.

Since I'm capable of handling it myself, I declined the installation service because, unfortunately, I'm not satisfied with the workmanship of most installation services.The first shock came the day after my purchase when I received a text message asking me to reschedule the service appointment initially set for March 11. The earliest available date was April 2— 44 days after my purchase! The second shock was realizing that the appliances didn't come with the necessary installation parts. I made this purchase through Best Buy's live web chat with a sales representative, opting only to exclude the installation labor. It never crossed my mind that these machines would arrive without such essential components. These weren't accessories but necessary parts for operation! The sales representative never warned me that I would need to purchase them separately. Moreover, the order confirmation screenshot sent by the representative clearly stated, “This item has services and parts included! ”The third shock happened on the scheduled service day. While randomly checking my Best Buy account, I noticed an open slot for March 14. I immediately rescheduled my appointment, and the service team confirmed via text message that they would arrive at 10 AM. I adjusted my schedule accordingly. However, Best Buy's partner, Lone Star Overnight (LSO), kept pushing back the service time— first to 11 AM, then 12 PM, and finally 1 PM. I couldn't wait at home any longer, so I had to leave, leaving my two daughters— one older and one younger— at home. The service team finally arrived at 1:26 PM, which I later confirmed through my security cameras.The fourth shock was the rudeness and carelessness of the service team. Even though my daughters asked the technician to wear shoe covers inside the house, he repeatedly stepped outside wearing them and then walked back in, which I could see from the cameras, along with the annoyed expression on his face. I also noticed that the appliances were delivered without packaging! (Could they have been display models and open box? ) Since I saw this on the cameras, I asked my daughters to closely monitor the technician and check for any visible damage. When I got home, my daughters told me that the technician struggled to move all three appliances by himself and that one machine scraped against the wall during transportation. However, since he didn't take our questions seriously, they hesitated to object and say, “We don't want this in this condition! ” Instead, they simply took a picture of the damage.The fifth shock came from the response of Best Buy's customer service representatives when I shared this terrible experience via text, phone calls, and web chat. • I was told, “We're handling it immediately, you'll be called today.” Yet, when Best Buy never called, these conversations continued with different representatives for three days, repeating the same sentences over and over. • Even after I sent a photo of the damaged machine still on the moving cart, one representative had the audacity to say, “How do we know you didn't do this? ” • I was told, “You need to bring the machine to us; we can't pick it up. Once you bring it in, you can receive a replacement.” • Despite the order stating, “This item has services and parts included” I was told, “Sorry, you have to purchase them” when I asked about the washer's hot and cold water inlet hoses and the dryer's power cord. For an additional cost that was only about 1% of the total purchase price, these sales representatives showed no effort or initiative to resolve a disappointed customer's frustration.In short, since we expected our new machines to arrive, we got rid of our old ones. Since that day, we haven't been able to do laundry at home.We are still waiting for our new machine.If I experienced all of this just during the initial purchase, I don't even want to imagine what I might go through during the five-year warranty period.It was a terrible experience. I think my next purchase won't be from Best Buy.

Sentence (English): I had my old Kenmore dishwasher for over 15 years.
Comments (English): [ Some good, some bad ] || ---------------- || I had my old Kenmore dishwasher for over 15 years. It was inexpensive and I never thought that it would last as long as it did. When it finally died I knew that I wanted a Bosch. I had read reviews and Consumer Reports and I was fine with paying a little more for the high quality of Bosch. The number one thing that I love about it is the fact that it's so quiet! If it wasn't for the red light that shines on the floor I wouldn't even know if it was running. I also love that it does a great job cleaning and drying the dishes. However, there are a few things that I don't like. I absolutely do not like the top utensil rack. I would much rather just drop my utensils into a basket than have to spend time lining them all up and making sure that they fit into a bunch of little grooves. Also, I'm having a difficult time getting the hang of how the dishes and bowls etc.fit into all the tines. I guess I just have to get used to it because it's very different from my old dishwasher. Even with these things that somewhat annoy me, I would still recommend Bosch dishwashers. They are definitely very attractive from the outside!

My quality of life has improved since getting this dishwasher. Sentence (English): You really have to buy one to understand why people call it "Dishwasher Auntie."
Comments (English): You really have to buy one to understand why people call it "Dishwasher Auntie." I recommend trying it out first rather than listening to people say things like "this doesn't work" or "this doesn't work." Since we live in a rented apartment, drilling holes was a hassle, so I looked for a no-drill model and bought this one because the reviews were so good. There is practically no installation involved; you just attach the drain pipe, place it on the stove, and use it right away. Seriously, all you need is the strength to lift the dishwasher, the eye to find the drain opening, and the hands to plug in the cord and press the button—that’s more than enough! At first, my wife and I wondered if we really needed a dishwasher for just the two of us, and if the 6-person model was too big. However, depending on whether you have large pots or pans, you can fit enough food for two or three meals in it with a bit of Tetris-style packing. For us, we don't need to pre-wash; we just fill a container with water, soak the dishes, and put them straight into the dishwasher to get them spotless! Since we were newlyweds, we used to feel awkward sitting alone while my wife or I did the dishes, so we'd talk or tidy up the house next to her. But now, we just tidy up briefly, run the dishwasher, and immediately grab a cup of coffee while chatting—that's it! It has an automatic door opening function, so by the time you return home, everything is already dry. (The water drains between the dishes to ensure complete drying, and while cups might pool slightly in the grooves on the bottom if placed flat, it’s not difficult to shake off.) It has various functions, and I’ve tried the Standard and Power modes so far. For items with grease, I tried the Standard mode but some residue remained, so I either soaked them well before putting them in, or I used the Power mode, which pre-cleans them effectively. (Since I’m a penny-pincher, I soak them in water to pre-clean them slightly before running the Standard mode for a clean finish.) I recommend this to anyone looking for a good dishwasher at an affordable price without needing to drill holes in their home.

Sentence (English): I recommend this to anyone looking for a good dishwasher at an affordable price without needing to drill holes in their home.
Comments (English): You really have to buy one to understand why people call it "Dishwasher Auntie." I recommend trying it out first rather than listening to people say things like "this doesn't work" or "this doesn't work." Since we live in a rented apartment, drilling holes was a hassle, so I looked for a no-drill model and bought this one because the reviews were so good. There is practically no installation involved; you just attach the drain pipe, place it on the stove, and use it right away. Seriously, all you need is the strength to lift the dishwasher, the eye to find the drain opening, and the hands to plug in the cord and press the button—that’s more than enough! At first, my wife and I wondered if we really needed a dishwasher for just the two of us, and if the 6-person model was too big. However, depending on whether you have large pots or pans, you can fit enough food for two or three meals in it with a bit of Tetris-style packing. For us, we don't need to pre-wash; we just fill a container with water, soak the dishes, and put them straight into the dishwasher to get them spotless! Since we were newlyweds, we used to feel awkward sitting alone while my wife or I did the dishes, so we'd talk or tidy up the house next to her. But now, we just tidy up briefly, run the dishwasher, and immediately grab a cup of coffee while chatting—that's it! It has an automatic door opening function, so by the time you return home, everything is already dry. (The water drains between the dishes to ensure complete drying, and while cups might pool slightly in the grooves on the bottom if placed flat, it’s not difficult to shake off.) It has various functions, and I’ve tried the Standard and Power modes so far. For items with grease, I tried the Standard mode but some residue remained, so I either soaked them well before putting them in, or I used the Power mode, which pre-cleans them effectively. (Since I’m a penny-pincher, I soak them in water to pre-clean them slightly before running the Standard mode for a clean finish.) I recommend this to anyone looking for a good dishwasher at an affordable price without needing to drill holes in their home.
